answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a relic as the anchor of the cost.
